items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Replaced Buck with the John Chilton Swing Kings at a place called 'Dog and Fox' in Wimbledon, the 30th.

ctx.x: Ben did some numbers alone with the rhythm section. There was one number that I would loved to have re-recorded, which was 'Satin Doll', but Jack Higgins insisted that some unknown girl singer he wanted to push perhaps, record a number and that did not leave time enough to do anything more. We had recorded the album between 9 a.m. and 1 p.m. The rhythm section had a T.V. date with Alex Welsch and could not stay any longer. I was not very satisfied with the "Satin Doll" version I did record.

The next day I played the 100 club and Nottingham the 29th. Replaced Buck with the John Chilton Swing Kings at a place called 'Dog and Fox' in Wimbledon, the 30th. Here was another surprise for me when I learned that John Chilton was a musician and a trumpet player to boot. When I did my first tour in England, John was collaborating with Jim Godbolt in the booking agency business. We had quite a few get togethers, but he never spoke about being a trumpet man or even a musician. And no one else ever mentioned it…

The only trouble I experienced during the tour and which was embarrassing for the orchestra and myself was the night we played in Blackpool, the 25th of May at the Casino Ballroom, which was located in an amusement park. Lily, Alan Littlejohn and myself arrived with Lew Hooper in his car. The rest of the gang had left London in a rented van as the English call a small bus, with the drums, bass and Alan's horn.
